physicalNotes: Radius 0.13837119 Jupiter radii from Egger et al. 2024 (2024A&A...688A.223E), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...688A.223E/abstract): 9,892.4 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.01415858 Jupiter masses (Egger et al. 2024, the mass the NASA Exoplanet Archive's composite table adopts (2024A&A...688A.223E), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...688A.223E/abstract) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Egger et al. 2024 (2024A&A...688A.223E), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname EGGER_ET_AL__2024): P 3.5379559 d
sources.shape: Egger et al. 2024 (2024A&A...688A.223E), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname EGGER_ET_AL__2024): a/R* 9.72; Damasso et al. 2023 (2023A&A...679A..33D), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname DAMASSO_ET_AL_2023): inclination 86.3 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Egger et al. 2024 (2024A&A...688A.223E), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname EGGER_ET_AL__2024): transit mid-time 2458471.36 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 10 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
